newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA DEPO RATES FALL AMID LOW DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA DEPO RATES FALL AMID LOW DEMAND.

text.p: Bulgaria's interbank deposit rates fell on Monday despite a rise in the central bank main interest rate and amid very low demand for funds, dealers said.

"Banks bid mainly for light volumes of short-term deposits because their liquidity is high at the moment. They offer money at very low interest to make some profit after the central bank ceased paying interest on their settlement accounts," one dealer said.
Interbank lev depo rates stood at 1.00-1.50 percent annually for periods between one day and a week, down from 1.50-3.0 percent on Friday.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 1.03 percent on Friday, lower than 1.80 percent on Thursday, a central bank official said.
The central bank last week raised its main lev interest rate to 5.59 percent annually from 5.50 percent, effective Monday.

Since July 14 the central bank has halted interest payments on banks' settlement accounts at the central bank in line with a cost saving programme under a restrictive fixed exchange rate regime known as a currency board system. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188
